newsitem.title: UK: LADBROKE RISES AFTER CASINO LICENCE AWARD.
newsitem.headline: LADBROKE RISES AFTER CASINO LICENCE AWARD.

text.p: Shares in British hotels to gaming company Ladbroke Group Plc rose on Tuesday as the market welcomed news of a new casino licence in London.
Ladbroke added 5p to 253.5p by 0955 GMT. The company said on Monday it had been granted a London casino licence to add to its four existing casinos in the British capital.

There has been market speculation that Ladbroke may bid for Capital Corporation Plc, which operates two up-market clubs in central London. Capital faced a hostile 190 million stg bid from London Clubs International earlier this year but the UK competition authorities vetoed any deal.
Ladbroke has declined comment on the speculation linking it with Capital Corp.
Analyst Greg Feehely of Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said the award of the London licence, the first new licence granted in the city for nine years, was "pretty positive" for Ladbroke.
He said it reinforced his view that a bid for Capital Corp was "not the only way for Ladbrokes to drive the casino business forward".
Ladbroke last month signed a letter of intent to acquire Colorado Gaming & Entertainment Co in an $85 million deal. Colorado Gaming operates three casinos in and around the city of Denver in the U.S.
Ladbroke is also bidding for three casino licences in South Africa and a decision on those applications is expected in the next few months.
A court case involving Ladbroke and national lottery operator Camelot is likely to conclude on Tuesday.
Camelot has taken out a private prosecution alleging that the "49s" numbers based betting game run by Ladbroke and fellow bookmakers William Hill and Coral is an illegal lottery.

Two previous attempts to have the game outlawed have ended in failure for Camelot. Although the case may conclude on Tuesday, it appears likely that the judge may reserve judgement to allow himself time to prepare a detailed explanation of his ruling.
